titleStmt.title: Autonomous closed-loop discovery of organic laser materials

abstract.p: We present a self-driving laboratory that combines robotic synthesis with Bayesian optimization to autonomously discover organic laser materials. The platform performs closed-loop experimentation across thousands of candidate molecules.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: The discovery of high-performance organic laser molecules has traditionally relied on intuition-driven synthesis followed by manual characterization. Closed-loop autonomous laboratories promise to compress this iteration cycle.

div.head: Methods
div.p: Our autonomous platform comprises a six-axis robotic arm, an on-line UV/Vis-fluorescence module, and a workflow orchestration layer based on the open-source ChemOS package. We integrate Bayesian optimization over a 12-dimensional reaction-condition space.
Each closed-loop experimentation cycle synthesizes one candidate, measures gain via amplified spontaneous emission, and updates the posterior.

div.head: Results
div.p: The closed-loop campaign converged within 482 experiments. We report six molecules with gain coefficients exceeding 80 cm^-1.

div.head: Discussion
div.p: This work demonstrates that closed-loop optimization combined with high-throughput experimentation can accelerate organic materials discovery by an order of magnitude.

figure.head: Figure 1
figure.figDesc: Autonomous closed-loop platform for materials discovery. The schematic shows the integration of robotic synthesis, automated characterization, and Bayesian optimization in a self-driving laboratory configuration.
